ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
title: Asiatic Lion population rises from 523 in 2015 to 891 in 2025; Reflects dedication of Forest Officials, Conservationists and Local Communities: Shri Bhupender Yadav
text:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau

Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

Asiatic Lion population rises from 523 in 2015 to 891 in 2025; Reflects dedication of Forest Officials, Conservationists and Local Communities: Shri Bhupender Yadav

On World Lion Day, Union Environment Minister reaffirms India’s commitment to Wildlife and Biodiversity Conservation

प्रविष्टि तिथि:
10 AUG 2026 12:02PM by PIB Delhi

On World Lion Day 2026, Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, celebrated India’s remarkable journey in lion conservation and reaffirmed the country’s unwavering commitment to protecting wildlife and biodiversity.

In a post on social media, the Minister noted that the Asiatic Lion population has steadily increased from 523 in 2015 to 891 in 2025. He attributed this achievement to the dedication of forest officials, conservationists, local communities and all those working tirelessly to protect the magnificent species.



🦁 On World Lion Day, we celebrate India’s remarkable journey in lion conservation.
India’s success in conserving the Asiatic Lion is a proud testament to our unwavering commitment to wildlife and biodiversity. From protecting critical habitats to strengthening conservation…
pic.twitter.com/7aJv98uRSG
— Bhupender Yadav (@byadavbjp)
August 10, 2026



Shri Yadav stated that India’s success in conserving the Asiatic Lion is a proud testament to the country’s commitment to wildlife and biodiversity. He reaffirmed the resolve to safeguard India’s natural heritage and ensure that the roar of the Asiatic Lion continues to resonate for generations to come.

On the occasion, in a social media post, Union MoS (EFCC), Shri Kirti Vardhan Singh, stated that by protecting critical habitats, strengthening conservation programmes and fostering coexistence, India has shown the world that development and nature can thrive together.



On
#WorldLionDay
, we honour India’s extraordinary journey in conserving the majestic Asiatic Lion.
From 523 lions in 2015 to 891 in 2025, this remarkable growth reflects the tireless efforts of forest officers, frontline workers, conservationists, local communities & countless…
pic.twitter.com/FCkRYqPwEI
— Kirti Vardhan Singh (@KVSinghMPGonda)
August 10, 2026



Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi announced 'Project Lion' on 15th August, 2020, to ensure long term conservation of the big cat. Currently, the lion range has expanded from around 30,000 sq. km. in 2020 to nearly 35,000 sq. km.

The project adopts a landscape-level, holistic approach to biodiversity conservation, emphasising habitat enhancement, disease monitoring and veterinary support, scientific population tracking, technology-aided interventions, biodiversity protection, benefit sharing and community involvement.
